fact_text: As of amendments to the Act on Foreign Nationals effective 8 July 2026, applications for a work permit are processed by the Directorate of Immigration (Utlendingastofnun), not the Directorate of Labour. A third-country professional still needs both a work permit and a separate residence permit.
evidence_quote: applications for work permits will be processed by the Directorate of Immigration.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed the employer files the work permit with the Directorate of Labour (Vinnumalastofnun). Actually since 8 July 2026 the Directorate of Immigration processes and issues work permits. Action: file the work permit together with the residence-permit application at the Directorate of Immigration.

fact_text: A third-country professional may not begin working in Iceland until BOTH a work permit and a residence permit have been granted. A signed job offer, or lawful presence in the country, does not by itself authorise starting work.
evidence_quote: A foreigner may not start working before a work permit and residence permit has been granted.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed you can start once you have arrived and signed a contract. Actually you may not start working before both the work permit and the residence permit are granted. Action: do not set a start date until both permits are issued.

fact_text: The work-based permit is tied to the specific employer it was granted for; the holder may not work for any other employer on that permit.
evidence_quote: The holder may not work for an employer other than the one to whom the work permit was granted.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed an Icelandic work permit lets you work for any employer. Actually it authorises work only for the employer it was granted to. Action: treat the permit as employer-specific; any other work needs a new permit first.

entity_title: Changing employer needs a new permit
fact_text: If a foreign national who holds a work permit wants to change jobs, they must apply for a new work permit from the new employer, resubmitting documents as if it were a new application (except educational documents).
evidence_quote: If a foreigner who has been issued a work permit and wants to change his/her job, he/she must apply for a work permit from the new employer.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed you can move to a new Icelandic employer freely once you hold a permit. Actually a new work permit must be granted for the new employer before you switch. Action: secure the new employer's work permit before changing jobs.

fact_text: A work permit on the basis of a shortage of labour may be granted only when no employee can be found on the Icelandic labour market or within the EEA/EFTA states or the Faroe Islands. (The expert-knowledge route is the alternative for qualified professionals.)
evidence_quote: shortage of labour may be granted when employees cannot be found either on the Icelandic labour market or within the EEA/EFTA member states or the Faroe Islands

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed any job offer qualifies a non-EEA hire. Actually a shortage-of-labour permit requires proof no worker is available in Iceland or the EEA/EFTA/Faroe Islands; qualified professionals instead use the expert-knowledge route. Action: confirm which basis applies before recruiting.

entity_title: Expert applicant may stay during processing
fact_text: An applicant for a residence permit for work requiring expert knowledge may be present in Iceland (if their stay is otherwise legal) while the application is submitted and processed - unlike shortage-of-labour applicants who need a visa, who may not be in Iceland during processing.
evidence_quote: Applicants for residence permits for work requiring expert knowledge may be present in Iceland when the application is submitted and while it is being processed, provided that their stay is legal.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed every non-EEA applicant must apply and wait from abroad. Actually expert-knowledge applicants may lawfully be in Iceland while processed, whereas visa-national shortage-of-labour applicants may not. Action: check your permit basis before planning arrival timing.

fact_text: A work-based residence permit applicant must independently demonstrate secure means of support of at least 259.951 ISK per month for an individual. Social assistance, alimony/child allowance, third-party support and cash are not accepted as secure support.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed the job offer alone proves you can support yourself. Actually you must show secure independent means of at least 259.951 ISK per month; welfare and third-party support do not count. Action: prepare income evidence covering the whole permit period.

entity_title: Permit revoked if domicile moves abroad
fact_text: A work-based residence permit is automatically revoked if the holder's Iceland-registered legal domicile is registered abroad for three months (and it can be revoked if the holder stays abroad more than three consecutive months).
evidence_quote: automatically revoked if his/her domicile, which was registered in Iceland, has been registered abroad for a period of three months.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed the permit stays valid until its printed expiry regardless of travel. Actually it is automatically revoked if your registered domicile moves abroad for three months. Action: keep your legal domicile in Iceland for the permit's duration.

fact_text: A work-based residence permit applicant must submit a certificate of private health insurance valid in Iceland for at least three months from the date their legal domicile is registered, with minimum coverage of ISK 2,000,000.
evidence_quote: for at least three months from the date of the registration of the applicant's legal domicile in Iceland, with a minimum coverage of ISK 2,000,000.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed Iceland's public health system covers you on arrival. Actually you must submit proof of private health insurance valid in Iceland for at least three months from legal-domicile registration, with minimum coverage of ISK 2,000,000. Action: buy compliant private cover before applying.

fact_text: After registering legal domicile in Iceland an individual generally waits 3 months before becoming covered by national (Iceland Health) health insurance; during that period they pay the full price for healthcare and must rely on private insurance.
evidence_quote: When an individual moves their legal domicile to Iceland, they generally have to wait 3 months before they become health insured in Iceland.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed you are publicly insured as soon as you register in Iceland. Actually national health insurance generally begins only 3 months after legal-domicile registration, and you pay full price meanwhile. Action: keep private insurance active through the 3-month waiting period.

fact_text: The kennitala (personal ID number) is allocated by Registers Iceland only after the residence permit is issued: the Directorate of Immigration requests domicile registration once the applicant has attended the photo appointment, submitted a residence notification and (if applicable) undergone a medical exam.
evidence_quote: Registers Iceland which allocates you a personal identification number (kennitala).

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed you can obtain a kennitala on arrival to open a bank account. Actually Registers Iceland allocates it only after the residence permit is issued and domicile is registered. Action: sequence banking and onboarding after the permit is granted.

fact_text: To register a legal domicile (logheimili) in Iceland, a non-EEA immigrant must already hold a residence permit and every immigrant must have a kennitala. Domicile registration must be with Registers Iceland if staying six months or longer.
evidence_quote: immigrants from outside the EEA must have a residence permit and all immigrants must have a national ID number

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed you register your address first and handle immigration later. Actually a non-EEA immigrant cannot register a legal domicile without a residence permit and a kennitala first. Action: obtain the residence permit and kennitala before registering domicile.

fact_text: After being granted a residence permit, the holder must attend the residence-card photo appointment, submit a residence notification and (if applicable) undergo a medical examination within 90 days, or the permit will not be issued - which can lead to illegal stay, expulsion and a re-entry ban.
evidence_quote: If you fail to attend a photo appointment, to notify your place of residence or undergo a medical examination within 90 days of being granted a residence permit, the permit will not be issued.

applies_to.non_obvious_note: Commonly believed the permit is final once approved. Actually you must complete the photo, residence notification and medical exam within 90 days of grant or the permit is not issued. Action: book the photo appointment and complete arrival steps immediately after approval.
